exposure: Midwifery caseload group practice (MCP) / continuity of care
cohort: The study included 3028 women with perinatal mental health conditions whose data was collected between 1st January 2018 and 31st January 2021.
finding: Women with perinatal mental health conditions receiving midwifery continuity of care had lower odds of preterm birth, higher odds of vaginal birth, and increased breastfeeding at discharge, with no difference in severe adverse neonatal outcomes, compared to those in standard care.
mod_finding: Women in midwifery caseload group practice had significantly higher odds of vaginal birth (adjOR 2.55, 95% CI 1.93-3.36) compared to those in standard care.
